scope: Independent geographic oracle adversarial audit; no production changes and no golden regeneration

corrected_findings.before: Wrapping native longitude 10.1 changed it to 10.099999999999994, misclassifying an exact boundary point as outside.
corrected_findings.after: Canonical longitudes remain unchanged; periodic queries continue to handle wrapping.

corrected_findings.before: Two boundaries at 0 and 1e-12 degrees longitude produced overlapping station brackets and erased the real middle-state interval.
corrected_findings.after: Only geometrically identical boundary events can merge. Distinct cuts that cannot be ordered within reported uncertainty fail certification instead of silently dropping mileage.

corrected_findings.before: A source on longitude 10.1 from latitude 0 to 0.5 incorrectly rejected a boundary segment on the same meridian ending at latitude 0 as unproved positive coincidence.
corrected_findings.after: Exact meridian/equator disjoint segments and zero-length touches are handled explicitly.

corrected_findings.before: A shallow latitude crossing of the (-0.1,40) to (0.1,40) geodesic understated station uncertainty: PROJ comparison differed by 0.000055640401114942506 m while the claimed bound was 0.0000021249991328222676 m.
corrected_findings.after: Coordinate evaluation allowance is converted to station uncertainty using a derivative lower bound; roots exceeding the 0.01 m cut target fail certification. The 2 micrometer minimum and all existing core expectations remain unchanged.

limitations: Coordinate evaluation allowance remains an explicit engineering assumption, not formal interval arithmetic proof.
Synthetic dateline and hole polygons test algorithms; they do not certify ownership of an actual Alaska, Hawaii, or boundary-hole fixture.
Unresolvable submicrometer visits are rejected instead of being promoted to complete goldens; the 10 cm real crossing and 3 cm exclusive offsets remain accepted.
